From the article:


What makes Merida’s science genuinely interesting is the mechanism itself. Most existing treatments for autoimmune conditions work by broadly suppressing the immune system, which can control symptoms but often leaves patients more vulnerable to infection and other side effects. Merida is developing biologics engineered to do something more precise, selectively identifying and eliminating the specific malfunctioning antibodies, known as autoantibodies, that are actually causing a given disease, while leaving the rest of the immune system intact.


That seems like a large sum to be paying for a Phase 1 biotech. One question that comes to mind was whether there is recent precedence for this.


$2.9B is certainly a lot to pay, but not unprecedented (see below).


Capstan and Aliada were all-cash and therefore genuinely $2.1bn / $1.4bn of committed value; Merida, Scorpion, Verve and Kate are "up to" figures. Until Lilly discloses the upfront (likely in the Q4 10-Q / closing accounting treatment ), Merida is not yet demonstrably a larger cash commitment than Capstan.
